title: Dishwashing at Thompson's and the stolen wallet at a theater rehearsal
summary: He washed dishes for $16 a week, then tried out for a show's pit band, where his pay was stolen from his pocket.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: we'll sort of get into it. Let's sort of get back to the beginnings of you're being in Pittsburgh. Did you get a job? A non-music job?

Yes, I had a job working at Thompson's Restaurant, dishwashing. And that I'll never forget. I earned -- I was making, what, $16.00 a week. And I got paid, and -- this was a little later, not too much later, because some show came in town. It was there, and they needed a trumpet player, so I went to the theater and sat in the pit to rehearse the show. They wanted to try me out and see if I was capable of playing the music, you know, the show, and the dancing girls. I'd never seen girls in tights and things before.
So I said man, this is it. You know?

I always did like the girls, you know? Oh yes. So I had my money in a wallet. Somebody took my wallet out of my hip pocket there while I was rehearsing, you know. And I felt back there for my wallet. I'd just gotten paid, and my $16.00 bucks is in there. Man, I almost died. And every since then I never put five cents in my wallet since.
Never! I have a wallet now --
You carry an empty wallet around?
No, well I haven't -- my wallet is fat, cards, all kinds of addresses and cards, and stuff, but not one five cents.
Well I won't ask you where you keep your money, though.
